channel.title: World Issues Today
channel.description: Today's most talked-about issues in Korea, the US, Japan, China and Europe, scored and linked to social media searches. Updated daily.

item.title: Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting: 16-year-old kills 3 children and a teacher
item.description: A 16-year-old opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Oct. 15 local time, killing three children and a teacher. The suspect was shot dead by a resident who followed him into the building.

item.title: Japan Meteorological Agency issues false ‘M9.9’ earthquake early warning, cancels it 8 minutes later; shinkansen halted
item.description: On the afternoon of Oct. 16, the Japan Meteorological Agency issued an earthquake early warning for a magnitude 9.9 quake across a wide area from Hokkaido to Tokai, then canceled it about eight minutes later. The actual quake was a magnitude 6.9 off the Kamchatka Peninsula, and part of the Tokaido Shinkansen was briefly halted.

item.title: Trump calls Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian refineries a ‘disgrace’ as clash erupts over Russian diesel deal
item.description: After the U.S. struck a diesel deal easing sanctions on Russian fuel, Ukraine broke the ‘energy truce’ on Oct. 15 and resumed attacks on Russian refineries. President Trump denounced it as a “disgrace,” while President Zelensky countered that the deal funds Putin’s war.

item.title: KOSPI plunges 7.6% on ‘Black Thursday’, triggering circuit breaker, then rebounds 2% a day later
item.description: South Korea’s KOSPI closed down 7.57% at 5,554.22 on Oct. 15 amid worries over the profitability of AI investment, as level-1 circuit breakers were triggered on both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ. On Oct. 16 the index rose 2.05% to 5,668.05, its first gain in eight sessions, though analysts remain cautious about a sustained recovery.

item.title: Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok puts impeachment of Chief Justice Jo Hee-dae on the table; PPP fires back with ‘impeach Lee Jae-myung’
item.description: Kim Min-seok, leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, said on Oct. 16 the party has begun discussing every option, including impeaching Supreme Court Chief Justice Jo Hee-dae. The opposition People Power Party countered that if an impeachment motion is filed, the public will cry ‘impeach Lee Jae-myung.’

item.title: Ship attacks mount in Strait of Hormuz as Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sinks
item.description: Amid the war with Iran, attacks on ships around the Strait of Hormuz have damaged more than 20 vessels this month. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sank after being hit by a projectile, and on Oct. 16 a tanker carrying Indian crew was also attacked.

item.title: Trump rules out nukes and ground troops in Iran, but plans ready for MOAB, largest non-nuclear bomb
item.description: President Trump said he will not use nuclear weapons against Iran and does not expect to send ground troops. The White House and Pentagon have reportedly drawn up plans to use the MOAB, the largest U.S. non-nuclear bomb, if ordered.

item.title: Apple’s first foldable ‘iPhone Duo’ sells out instantly in China presale, resale markups top 7,000 yuan
item.description: The first batch of Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, sold out almost immediately after presales opened in China on the night of Oct. 16. On secondhand platforms, it is listed at more than 7,000 yuan above retail.

item.title: U.S. AI and chip stocks tumble as 5% Treasury yields stoke AI funding fears; Apple tops $5 trillion
item.description: AI and semiconductor stocks sank as Treasury yields above 5% fueled worries about the cost of AI infrastructure spending, with the Nasdaq falling 1.88% on Oct. 14. Markets steadied on Oct. 15 as the Dow rose more than 1%, and Apple’s market value was reported to have topped $5 trillion.

item.title: Bucheon paint factory fire injures 8 including 6 firefighters, 2 seriously
item.description: A fire broke out on the morning of Oct. 16 at a metal parts coating factory in Naedong, Ojeong District, Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province, injuring six firefighters and two factory workers. Two of the injured firefighters are in serious condition, and one was taken to hospital in cardiac arrest.

item.title: Incheon Guwol-dong stabbing: 59-year-old Choi Chung-rak arrested and named; 8 injured
item.description: Choi Chung-rak, 59, who injured eight people in a knife attack at a large shopping complex in Guwol-dong, Namdong District, Incheon, on Oct. 13, was formally arrested and publicly identified on Oct. 16. A 19-year-old woman among the victims has yet to regain consciousness.

item.title: Mie becomes first Japanese prefecture to pass customer harassment ordinance with penalties of up to ¥500,000
item.description: The Mie Prefectural Assembly on Oct. 16 unanimously passed Japan’s first customer harassment (‘kasuhara’) ordinance with penalties. Violating a governor’s prohibition order could bring a fine of up to 500,000 yen, and the ordinance takes effect in April 2027.

item.title: Tesla unveils second-generation Roadster, ‘flying car’ demo leaps over 5 cars on thrusters
item.description: Tesla unveiled its second-generation Roadster at a SpaceX test site in Texas on Oct. 15, showing it clearing five Tesla vehicles using thrusters. Production is slated for 2028, but no price or release date has been announced.

item.title: French high school education protests spread to Albania, Greece and Argentina
item.description: High school protests that began in France over overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages are spreading to Albania, Greece and Argentina. More than 6,000 people have been arrested in France, 85% of them under 18.

item.title: Albania student protests escalate for 4th day, opposing Kushner resort and demanding PM Rama resign
item.description: Student-led anti-government protests in the Albanian capital Tirana have entered a fourth day and are growing more heated. Protesters are denouncing corruption and neglect of education, opposing a coastal resort project backed by Jared Kushner, and calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

item.title: PM Takaichi’s remark that makeup and chores take her ‘3 to 4 hours more than a male PM’ sparks backlash
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told the Diet she spends three to four hours more than a male prime minister on things like makeup and morning chores, igniting a debate over gender roles. Opposition lawmakers criticized the answer as diminishing the status of women.

item.title: EU-Gulf summit in Riyadh postponed after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; Aden presidential palace also hit
item.description: The Gulf Cooperation Council postponed the EU-GCC summit set for Oct. 24 in Riyadh, citing repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Houthis also attacked the presidential palace in Aden, Yemen, killing five people.

item.title: China’s September chip exports jump 136% to $45 billion while volume rises just 1%
item.description: China’s integrated circuit exports hit a record of about $44.95 billion in September, up 136% from a year earlier. Volume rose only 1%, with higher memory prices driven by AI demand accounting for most of the increase.

item.title: Overseas Koreans Agency to move to Sejong as 44 capital-area agencies relocate; Incheon pushes back
item.description: The Ministry of the Interior and Safety’s second plan to move central government bodies to Sejong includes 44 agencies in the Seoul metropolitan area, among them the Overseas Koreans Agency. Opposition is growing in Incheon after the agency, which opened in Songdo in 2023, was listed for priority relocation in the first half of 2027.

item.title: 1,200 queue overnight for Chiikawa merch at Seoul’s Yongsan store as resale prices spark backlash
item.description: Fans lined up overnight ahead of a new merchandise drop at the Chiikawa shop in Seoul’s Yongsan I’Park Mall, with more than 1,200 people in line at the peak. Limited-edition keychains are being resold at more than five times retail, prompting calls for a reservation system.

item.title: President Lee Jae-myung’s approval rebounds 2 points to 39%, disapproval at 52% (Gallup Korea)
item.description: President Lee Jae-myung’s job approval rose 2 percentage points to 39% in Gallup Korea’s third-week October poll. Disapproval also rose 1 point to 52%, with real estate policy the most cited reason.
